name: Lincoln Memorial
description: The great marble temple at the west end of the Mall, with the seated Lincoln and his two most famous speeches carved on the walls. The view east over the Reflecting Pool is the city's classic picture.
tips: Open 24 hours, every day. Rangers are on duty from 9:30 a.m. to 10 p.m.
Come back after dark: the memorial is lit and much quieter.
Nearest Metro: Foggy Bottom, about a 15 to 20 minute walk.

access.note: A wide flight of steps up the front. Ask a ranger about the accessible entrance.

name: Washington Monument

price.text: Free · $1 online booking fee per ticket

lead_time: Book ahead: tickets open online 30 days before at 10 a.m. Eastern, plus a day-before release.
description: The marble obelisk at the center of the Mall. An elevator takes about 70 seconds to the top, with views over the city, the river and Virginia.
tips: Free, but everyone 2 and older needs a timed ticket. Online tickets have a $1 booking fee.
Online tickets open 30 days ahead at 10 a.m. Eastern, with more released the day before. Make a recreation.gov account early.
Free same-day tickets at the Washington Monument Lodge on 15th Street from 8:45 a.m., while they last. Expect a line.
Closes one day a month for maintenance, on July 4 and Dec 25, and in high wind or storms. Check the alerts on nps.gov/wamo.
closed_note: Closed Dec 25 and one day a month for maintenance

access.note: The visit is by elevator. Waiting outside before your time can be cold and windy.

name: World War II and Vietnam Veterans Memorials
description: Two very different memorials a short walk apart: the fountains and granite pillars of the World War II Memorial, and the black wall of the Vietnam Veterans Memorial, cut into the ground with more than 58,000 names.
tips: Open 24 hours and free.
Walk them on the way from the Washington Monument to the Lincoln Memorial.

name: Tidal Basin memorials: MLK, FDR and Jefferson
description: Three memorials around the Tidal Basin: Martin Luther King Jr. carved from a block of granite, the outdoor rooms of the FDR Memorial, and the domed Jefferson Memorial across the water.
tips: Open 24 hours and free.
A walk around the water links all three. Allow an hour or more.
Beautiful at night, when the Jefferson Memorial is lit.

access.note: Flat but long. Cold and windy by the water in November.

name: The White House from Lafayette Square
description: See the north front from Lafayette Square, or the south front from the Ellipse. The White House Visitor Center nearby has exhibits and a short film.
tips: Tours for international visitors can only be requested through your embassy, well ahead, and are not guaranteed.
White House Visitor Center: 1450 Pennsylvania Avenue NW.
Security zones change often; follow the signs and the officers' directions.

name: National Air and Space Museum
lead_time: Reserve free timed passes before you go; same-day passes go fast.
description: The Wright Flyer, Apollo 11's command module and a huge gallery of aircraft and spacecraft. After a decade of renovation, its last galleries reopened in fall 2026.
tips: Free, but everyone needs a free timed-entry pass for the DC museum.
A limited batch of same-day passes is released online each morning at 8:30 a.m. Eastern.
Enter on Jefferson Drive, the National Mall side.
Open 10 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. daily except Dec 25.

name: National Museum of African American History and Culture
lead_time: Reserve free timed passes before you go.
description: A deeply moving museum that starts underground with the history of slavery and rises to music, sport and culture. Plan at least three hours.
tips: Free, but everyone of any age needs a free timed-entry pass.
Advance passes open 30 days ahead at 8 a.m. Eastern; same-day passes go online at 8:15 a.m.
Open 10 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. Tuesday to Sunday, and noon to 5:30 p.m. on Monday. Closed Dec 25.
Start at the bottom, in the history galleries, then work your way up.

access.note: Step-free with elevators. The history galleries are crowded and emotionally heavy.

name: National Museum of Natural History
description: Dinosaurs, the Hope Diamond, a life-size whale and the ocean hall, under a great rotunda with an African elephant.
tips: Free, no pass needed.
Busiest at midday and on weekends; go at opening.

name: National Museum of American History
description: The Star-Spangled Banner that inspired the anthem, first ladies' gowns, presidents and pop culture. A good rainy-day museum.
tips: Free, no pass needed.

name: National Gallery of Art
description: Old masters in the West Building, including the only Leonardo da Vinci painting in the Americas, and modern art in the I. M. Pei East Building, linked by an underground walkway.
tips: Always free, no pass needed.
Open 10 a.m. to 5 p.m.
The Sculpture Garden next door is good for a break.

name: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum

price.text: Free · no pass needed Sept to Feb

description: The national memorial to the Holocaust, told through objects, photographs and survivors' voices. A powerful, demanding visit.
tips: Free. From September to February no pass is needed for the permanent exhibition.
Open daily 10 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. Closed Yom Kippur and Dec 25.
Recommended for ages 11 and up; a separate exhibition, Daniel's Story, is for younger visitors.

access.note: Step-free. The permanent exhibition is graphic in places.

name: US Capitol tour
lead_time: Reserve a tour time online; same-day passes may be available.
description: A free guided tour of the Crypt, the Rotunda under the dome and National Statuary Hall, starting at the underground Capitol Visitor Center.
tips: Tours are free. Reserving a time is recommended, not required.
Open Monday to Saturday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The last tour starts at 3:20 p.m.
No reservation? Arrive early, and no later than 2:30 p.m., for a same-day pass.
Check the prohibited items list before you go; security is airport-style.
closed_note: Closed Sundays, Thanksgiving, Dec 25, Jan 1 and Inauguration Day

access.note: The visitor center and tour route are fully accessible.

name: Library of Congress
lead_time: Reserve a free timed ticket; same-day tickets go online at 9 a.m.
description: The Thomas Jefferson Building: a dazzling marble Great Hall, mosaics and a balcony view down into the domed Main Reading Room. Across the street from the Capitol.
tips: Free, but you need a free timed-entry ticket.
Tickets open 30 days ahead; free same-day tickets go online each day at 9 a.m. Eastern.
Open Tuesday to Saturday, 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., to 8 p.m. on Thursdays. Closed Sundays and Mondays.
Easy to pair with a Capitol tour: a tunnel links the two buildings.
closed_note: Closed Sundays, Mondays and some federal holidays

name: Eastern Market
description: A brick market hall from 1873 with butchers, bakers, cheese and a lunch counter. On weekends, farmers, craft and flea stalls fill the street outside.
tips: Indoor South Hall: Tuesday to Friday 7 a.m. to 7 p.m., Saturday 7 a.m. to 6 p.m., Sunday 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.
Weekends are the liveliest, with the outdoor stalls.
Eastern Market Metro is a short walk away.

food.note: Lots of choice: sandwiches, crab cakes, pastries and fruit.

name: Union Market
description: A big, bright food hall with more than 40 local vendors, from tacos and ramen to oysters and cookies. La Cosecha, a Latin American market, is across the street.
tips: Open Monday to Saturday 8 a.m. to 9 p.m., Sunday 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Each stall sets its own hours.
A short ride from Union Station, or about 15 minutes' walk from NoMa-Gallaudet Metro.

food.note: Many kitchens under one roof, so everyone finds something. Ask each stall about ingredients.

name: Ben's Chili Bowl
description: A U Street landmark since 1958, famous for its chili half-smoke. The original diner reopened in May 2026 after a long restoration, with its old counter and booths kept.
tips: Open until 4 a.m. on Friday and Saturday nights.
Across from the U Street Metro station.
Expect a line at busy times; it moves fast.

food.note: Ask which sausages and chili contain pork; the menu has other choices.

name: Georgetown and the C&O Canal
description: The city's oldest neighborhood: brick Federal houses, cobbled side streets, shops along M Street and a towpath beside the old canal, down to the river and the waterfront park.
tips: No Metro stop: walk from Foggy Bottom station, or take a bus or ride.
Walk the quiet residential streets north of M Street, then down to the waterfront.

access.note: Brick sidewalks and some steep streets up from the river.

name: The Wharf
description: A waterfront promenade with restaurants, piers and the Municipal Fish Market, a historic open-air seafood market. A good evening stroll.
tips: Free to walk. Waterfront Metro is a few minutes away.
Easy to pair with the Tidal Basin memorials, a walk to the west.

name: Arlington National Cemetery
description: The national military cemetery across the river: rows of white headstones, the Kennedy graves and the Changing of the Guard at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier.
tips: Free. Open daily 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. from October to March.
The Changing of the Guard is every hour, on the hour, from October to March.
Metro Blue Line to Arlington Cemetery station, right by the welcome center.
An active cemetery with daily funerals: be quiet and respectful.
how: Metro Blue Line to Arlington Cemetery

access.note: Hilly and spread out. A paid tram tour saves the walking.

name: Old Town Alexandria
description: An 18th-century river town of brick rowhouses, shops and restaurants along King Street, down to the Potomac waterfront.
tips: Take Metro to King Street-Old Town, then the free King Street Trolley down to the river.
The trolley runs every 15 minutes, 11 a.m. to 11 p.m., every day.
how: Metro Blue or Yellow Line to King Street-Old Town, then the free trolley

name: George Washington's Mount Vernon

price.text: $30 adults · $16 ages 6 to 11 · 5 and under free

lead_time: Buy tickets online for a good Mansion tour time.
description: George Washington's home and farm above the Potomac: the mansion, gardens, a working farm and the tombs of George and Martha Washington, with an honest look at the enslaved people who lived and worked here.
tips: Adults $30, ages 6 to 11 $16, 5 and under free. Parking is free.
Open every day of the year; 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. from November to March.
Buy online for the best Mansion tour time; on busy days the next tour can be hours away.
By public transport: Metro Yellow Line to Huntington, then the Fairfax Connector bus.
how: About 30 to 45 minutes by car or ride app; or Metro and bus

access.note: Gravel paths and a fair amount of walking between buildings.

name: Udvar-Hazy Center (Air and Space)
description: Air and Space's giant hangars near Dulles airport: Space Shuttle Discovery, an SR-71 Blackbird, a Concorde and hundreds of aircraft.
tips: Free, no passes needed. Open 10 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. daily except Dec 25.
Parking is $15, free after 4 p.m.
Good on the way to or from a flight at Dulles.
how: By car or ride app, about 10 minutes from Dulles airport

name: Tatte Bakery & Cafe, Bethesda
description: A bright bakery cafe steps from Bethesda Row: pastries, shakshuka, breakfast sandwiches and salads, from early morning.
tips: Good for: breakfast, coffee, a quick lunch.
Open Monday to Saturday 7 a.m. to 8 p.m., Sunday 8 a.m. to 7 p.m.
7276 Wisconsin Avenue.

food.note: Lots of vegetarian dishes. Ask about ingredients at the counter.

name: PopUp Bagels
description: New in Bethesda in 2026: warm 'rip and dip' bagels with signature schmears. A fast breakfast on the way to work.
tips: Good for: breakfast to go.
7607 Old Georgetown Road.

name: Dalia's Falafel
description: Began as a pop-up: falafel bowls, pita and kebabs with a clean-eating focus. A light, quick lunch.
tips: Good for: weekday lunch.
7750 Old Georgetown Road.

name: Six Ways to Sunday
description: A small Sino-Siamese spot with fusion plates inspired by Bangkok's late-night food culture.
tips: Good for: dinner with a friend or two.
8003 Norfolk Avenue.

food.note: Ask which dishes contain pork or shellfish.

name: Agora Bethesda
description: Mezze from Turkey, Greece and Lebanon under the Hyatt Regency, right above Bethesda Metro. Opened in July 2026; the third Agora after DC and Tysons.
tips: Good for: dinner, a group meal, weekend brunch (bottomless brunch option).
1 Bethesda Metro Center, at Wisconsin Avenue.
Book a table for weekend evenings and brunch.

food.note: Lots of shared plates, many vegetarian. Ask about halal meat and alcohol in sauces.

name: Pisco y Nazca
description: Modern Peruvian: eight ceviches, lomo saltado and fusion dishes, with pisco sours.
tips: Good for: a lively lunch or dinner.
7401 Woodmont Avenue.

food.note: Seafood-forward; meat dishes too. Ask what contains pork.

name: Mon Ami Gabi
description: A long-running, recently renovated French bistro on Bethesda Row: steak frites and onion soup.
tips: Good for: a relaxed dinner after a walk on Bethesda Row.
7239 Woodmont Avenue.

name: The Food Market
description: Chef Chad Gauss's comfort-food restaurant with mixed cuisines and a long cocktail list. Made for a long sit-down.
tips: Good for: a celebration dinner.
4720 Hampden Lane.

name: Bethesda Row
description: Bethesda's walkable shopping and dining streets around Bethesda Avenue and Woodmont Avenue, with fashion and lifestyle shops, cafes and restaurants.
tips: Good for: an evening stroll after work, or Saturday shopping.
The free Bethesda Circulator stops nearby.

name: Capital Crescent Trail to Georgetown

price.source: National Park Service and the Coalition for the Capital Crescent Trail

description: A paved, 7-mile rail trail through the trees from downtown Bethesda to the Georgetown waterfront. Gently downhill toward Georgetown.
tips: Good for: a weekend morning walk, run or bike ride.
The trailhead is on Bethesda Avenue, just west of Woodmont Avenue.
Rent a Capital Bikeshare bike in Bethesda (station at Woodmont Avenue and Strathmore Street) and ride down to Georgetown.
In Georgetown the trail ends at Water Street NW, near the waterfront.

access.note: Paved and wide. It climbs gently on the way back to Bethesda.

name: Round House Theatre
description: Bethesda's well-loved theater, celebrating its 50th anniversary, with new plays and many Helen Hayes Award nominations.
tips: Good for: an evening out without going into DC.
4545 East-West Highway, a short walk from Bethesda Metro.
Check the season and buy tickets ahead.

name: Strathmore
description: A concert hall and historic mansion beside Grosvenor-Strathmore Metro: orchestras, touring artists and jazz in the Music Center, smaller concerts, exhibitions and afternoon teas in the Mansion.
tips: Good for: an evening concert.
Two stops north of Bethesda on the Red Line; a covered sky bridge links the Metro garage to the Music Center.
5301 Tuckerman Lane. Check strathmore.org for the calendar.

access.note: Step-free from the Metro garage across the sky bridge.

name: McCrillis Gardens
description: A quiet five-acre garden with walking paths, gazebos and benches. A peaceful break close to downtown Bethesda.
tips: Good for: a quiet morning or a lunchtime walk.
6910 Greentree Road.

name: Glen Echo Park
description: A former amusement park on the Potomac, now an arts park run with the National Park Service: Art Deco buildings, studios, galleries and dances in the historic Spanish Ballroom.
tips: Good for: a weekend afternoon.
Grounds open daily 6 a.m. to 1 a.m. Free entry and free parking.
The 1921 Dentzel carousel runs in the warmer months, not in November.
Check glenechopark.org for social dances and events.
how: About 15 minutes by car or ride app from downtown Bethesda

name: Great Falls (C&O Canal, Maryland side)
description: The Potomac pours through a rocky gorge just outside the city. From Great Falls Tavern, walk along the old canal and out to the overlooks.
tips: $20 per car, valid 7 days and also at Great Falls Park in Virginia. Card only at the entrance.
Grounds open during daylight. From November to February the visitor center is closed Monday to Wednesday.
Wear good shoes: rocky paths, and the river is dangerous. Stay behind the barriers.
how: About 25 minutes by car or ride app from Bethesda; no Metro

access.note: Flat towpath to the canal, rocky paths to the overlooks.

name: Washington National Cathedral
description: A vast Gothic cathedral on a hill, with stained glass, carved stone and views over the city. On Wisconsin Avenue between Bethesda and Georgetown.
tips: Sightseeing admission: $12 adults, $8 ages 5 to 17, 4 and under free.
Sightseeing most Mondays to Saturdays; Sundays are for worship. Events can close it, so check the visiting page first.
Buy online up to 24 hours ahead, or at the door.
Nearest Metro: Tenleytown or Woodley Park, about 1.5 miles away. A ride app is easier.

name: Big Bus hop-on hop-off tour
description: Open-top double-decker buses loop past the memorials, museums and the Capitol with recorded commentary in several languages. Hop off where you like and catch a later bus.
tips: Online tickets from $54 for 24 hours (full price $65); 48 and 72 hour tickets cost more.
In winter, buses come every 30 to 45 minutes; the first bus is around 9:30 a.m. and the last around 4:30 p.m.
Big Bus also runs a 2-hour panoramic night tour.
Union Station is on the Red Line, direct from Bethesda. Track the buses in the Big Bus app.

access.note: The open top deck is cold in November; sit downstairs if needed.

name: Monuments by Moonlight night tour
area: Union Station or Washington Welcome Center

price.source: Old Town Trolley Tours via Tripster and Travelocity listings

lead_time: Book ahead; popular nights sell out.
description: A 2.5-hour trolley tour with a live guide after dark, with stops to walk up to the lit memorials, including MLK and FDR, Lincoln, Vietnam and Korean War.
tips: Departs at 7:30 p.m. from Union Station or the Washington Welcome Center, 1001 E Street NW. About $60 per adult.
Runs nightly except July 4, Thanksgiving and Dec 25.
A good way to see the memorials at night without walking alone.
closed_note: No tours July 4, Thanksgiving and Dec 25

name: Virginia wine country group tour
description: Join a small-group day tour to Northern Virginia's wineries: transport, a guide and tastings at two or three wineries, without driving.
tips: Spirited Tours (listed by Destination DC): group tours with a certified wine guide, pickups in DC at L'Enfant Plaza and at Ballston and Vienna Metro stations.
Vineyard Voyages: 6 to 7 hour day trips from DC or Leesburg, from $99.
Tastings and lunch are often extra; check what each tour includes.
Group tours sell single seats, so they work well on your own.
how: Tour bus or van with pickup in DC or at a Metro station

access.note: 21 and over for tastings. Bring ID.

name: Philadelphia by train
description: The Liberty Bell, Independence Hall and Reading Terminal Market, a simple day trip by train from Union Station.
tips: Amtrak Northeast Regional takes about 2 hours, Acela about 1 hour 40 minutes, with many trains a day.
Union Station is on the Red Line, direct from Bethesda.
Book Amtrak ahead for lower fares; holiday weekends fill up early.
how: Amtrak from Union Station to Philadelphia 30th Street

name: Baltimore by train
description: The Inner Harbor waterfront, the National Aquarium and Fells Point's old streets and seafood.
tips: Amtrak Northeast Regional is about 40 minutes from Union Station, Acela about 30.
Then a short ride from Baltimore Penn Station to the harbor.
how: Amtrak from Union Station to Baltimore Penn Station

name: Harpers Ferry, West Virginia
description: A historic river town where the Potomac and Shenandoah meet, now a national historical park with hiking and views. About 70 miles from DC.
tips: Trains don't allow a same-day round trip (MARC runs weekdays only, Amtrak once a day), so go by car, ride app or a guided tour.
Wear good shoes for the steep streets and trails.
how: By car (about 1.5 hours) or a guided day tour

access.note: Steep, uneven streets and stone steps.

name: Potomac dinner cruises from The Wharf

price.text: from about $106 (Odyssey); Spirit of Washington around $170

lead_time: Book ahead; weekend and holiday sailings fill up.
description: City Cruises' evening cruises on the Potomac past the lit monuments, the Georgetown waterfront and the Jefferson and Lincoln memorials. Two styles: the elegant Odyssey, with a three-course plated dinner under glass, or the livelier Spirit of Washington, with a buffet and a DJ.
tips: Odyssey: about 2.5 to 3 hours, from about $106. It sails under the low bridges for close-up views, and the dining rooms are climate-controlled, so it runs in any weather.
Spirit of Washington: about 2 to 2.5 hours with buffet and dancing, around $170.
Departs from Pier 4, 580 Water Street SW. Boarding starts 30 to 60 minutes before; check your ticket.
From Bethesda: Red Line to Gallery Place, then the Green Line to Waterfront, two blocks from the pier.
Tickets are sold per person with a table for your party, so it works well on your own. Drinks are extra.

name: Spirit of Baltimore dinner cruise
description: A 2.5-hour evening cruise on Baltimore's Inner Harbor and the Patapsco River: buffet dinner, a DJ, and the city skyline lit up from the rooftop deck.
tips: From about $94. Coffee and tea are included; other drinks are extra.
Departs from 561 Light Street, Inner Harbor. Boarding starts 30 minutes before.
City Cruises sails from Baltimore all year.
Pair it with a day in Baltimore by train, and check the last train back to Union Station before you book.

name: Potomac sightseeing cruise and water taxi
description: A shorter, cheaper way onto the river: narrated sightseeing cruises past the monuments, or the water taxi between The Wharf, Georgetown, Old Town Alexandria and National Harbor.
tips: Sightseeing cruises leave from the Transit Pier, 970 Wharf Street SW; dinner cruises use Pier 4.
Fewer departures in the cold months. Check the day's schedule before you go.

access.note: Open decks are cold in November; dress warmly.
